title: Amidst fears of AI cyberattacks, Satya Nadella says lots of critical infrastructure is ‘unpatchable’
lede: At the DealBook Summit, Satya Nadella warned that much critical infrastructure runs on firmware that cannot be patched, from data center chillers to HVAC and transport systems, yet sits on the internet.

points: He named firmware, chillers and HVAC as connected systems that cannot be fixed and are now exposed to AI-assisted attacks.
He put the recent global Outlook outage down to a latent bug that set off a perfect storm, and said Microsoft will fix both architecture and operations.
Outages at the NSA, FAA and Apple have fed suspicion of cyberattacks, which officials have denied.
AI now finds vulnerabilities quickly, he said, which removes the time companies once had to test patches.
Patches must reach production as soon as they exist because flaws are exploited in the wild, and he expects that to cause instability.

sections.text: Faster AI-driven vulnerability discovery shrinks patch windows, so teams shipping software need release and rollback processes that can push urgent fixes without breaking production.
